title: Shape catalog + Dedicated tier mapping in control plane (config + validation + migration)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
- Dedicated tiers (Standard / Performance / Premium) require enforceable, machine-readable constraints: which hardware shapes are valid per tier, and which region/availability restrictions apply.
- Today we have shape info spread across:
  - Infra provisioning templates
  - ad-hoc sales/SRE docs
  - per-customer overrides in deployment config
- Result: sales proposals, provisioning, and runtime enforcement diverge.

Goal
Represent a canonical Dedicated hardware shape catalog and a tier->shape mapping in the control plane, and enforce validation for:
1) new Dedicated deployments
2) tier changes (upgrades/downgrades)
3) region moves / capacity migrations

Non-goals
- Changing provisioning pipeline internals (handled elsewhere).
- Defining throughput numbers (comes from PRD + pricing docs).

Proposed approach (v1)
1) Add canonical Shape Catalog to control plane config
   - New entity: dedicated_shape
   - Primary key: shape_id (string, stable; e.g., "l4-1x", "a100-80gb-1x", "h100-80gb-8x-nvlink")
   - Core attributes to store (v1):
     - gpu_type, gpu_count
     - mig_profile ("none" | profile string)
     - cpu_cores, ram_gb
     - nic_gbps
     - local_ssd_gb (if applicable)
     - nvlink_required (bool)
     - notes (free-form)
   - Ownership: Eng Infra provides source-of-truth values; control plane is the distribution point for enforcement + downstream tooling.

2) Add Dedicated Tier Mapping
   - New entity: dedicated_tier_policy (versioned)
   - Fields (v1):
     - tier_name (standard|performance|premium)
     - allowed_shape_ids (list)
     - region_allowlist (list of region codes)
     - burst_allowed (bool) + max_burst_multiplier (if applicable; policy-level, used by admission control)
     - maintenance_policy_ref (string; points to runbook/doc section)
   - Rationale: tiers need to be enforceable by config validation and referenced by runtime/SRE tooling.

3) Validation rules (create/update time)
   - Dedicated deployment must reference either:
     (a) shape_id directly, OR
     (b) tier + requested_shape_id (if we want explicit shape selection within tier)
   - Validation:
     - shape_id must exist in catalog
     - tier must exist
     - shape_id must be in tier.allowed_shape_ids
     - deployment.region must be in tier.region_allowlist
     - if shape has mig_profile != none, block for tiers that disallow MIG (policy knob if needed)
   - Failure mode:
     - hard error on create/update; include actionable message for Sales/CS ("h100-80gb-8x-nvlink not available in eu-west-1 for Premium; supported regions: us-east-1, us-west-2")

4) API/UX impacts
   - Control plane API additions:
     - GET /v1/dedicated/shapes (internal + Terraform)
     - GET /v1/dedicated/tiers (internal + Console)
     - Deployment response should include resolved shape metadata (gpu_type/count) for visibility.
   - Console minimal UI work is tracked separately (DES-144), but we should ensure the API provides:
     - tier_name
     - shape_id
     - region
     - policy_version

Migration plan
Phase 0: Schema + read-path (no enforcement)
- Land DB schema + config loading for shape catalog + tier mapping.
- Backfill existing Dedicated deployments with shape_id where possible:
  - Map from legacy fields (gpu_type, gpu_count, instance_type) -> shape_id.
  - For ambiguous cases, set shape_id = "legacy-unknown" and emit audit event + Slack alert to #eng-infra for manual follow-up.

Phase 1: Soft validation
- Gate new enforcement behind feature flag: dedicated_shape_catalog_validation_v1.
- Enable in staging + internal dogfood Dedicated deployments.
- Emit warnings (not blocking) for invalid combos to build confidence.

Phase 2: Hard validation + cleanup
- Turn on blocking validation for new creates/updates.
- Keep grandfathered deployments allowed but disallow tier changes until shape_id is resolved.
- Add an admin tool/endpoint to fix up legacy deployments (one-time).

Phase 3: Remove legacy fields
- Deprecate old per-deployment gpu fields from the config schema once adoption >95%.

Rollout plan
- Week 1: implement schema, shape_id mapping util, read APIs.
- Week 2: staging enablement + dogfood; start Terraform integration.
- Week 3: hard validation for new deployments; migration cleanup.

Test plan
- Unit tests for validation matrix:
  - invalid tier
  - unknown shape_id
  - shape not allowed for tier
  - region not allowed
  - MIG disallowed
- Integration tests:
  - create Dedicated deployment in staging using known-good shape
  - attempt invalid create and verify error message is sales/CS readable
- Migration tests:
  - backfill job produces deterministic shape_ids
  - audit events created for ambiguous legacy deployments

Operational considerations
- Versioning: policy_version must be stored on the deployment so SRE can understand which mapping applied at creation time.
- Metrics/logging:
  - control_plane.validation_failures_total{reason,tier,shape,region}
  - migration.legacy_shape_unmapped_total{region}
- Oncall: validation failures should not page, but should create an internal alert if >X/min (suggest X=10/min) to detect bad Terraform rollout.

Links / references
- Confluence (shape catalog): sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/dedicated-hardware-shapes-catalog.json
- Confluence (tier definitions): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-tier-definitions.json
- ADR (tiering/burst semantics): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0128-tiering-model-and-burst-policy.json
- Terraform exposure work: sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr-412.json

Open questions
1) Do we want tier to imply an automatic shape selection ("best available") or require explicit shape choice within tier?
   - Proposal for v1: require explicit shape_id for now; can add auto-selection later.
2) How do we represent temporary supply restrictions (e.g., Premium shape unavailable in region for 2 weeks)?
   - Proposal: tier policy includes region_allowlist; Infra updates policy_version and SRE communicates via status page / internal announce.
3) Are we okay with grandfathering legacy deployments that can’t be mapped immediately?
   - Proposal: yes, but block tier upgrades until resolved to avoid contractual mismatch.

Acceptance criteria
- Control plane stores and serves a canonical shape catalog and tier mapping.
- New Dedicated deployment create/update fails fast for invalid tier/shape/region combos when flag enabled.
- Existing deployments are backfilled with shape_id (>=95% success), with a clear list of unmapped cases.
- Terraform consumers can read the catalog/mapping (or at minimum validate inputs using the API) without hardcoding shape lists.
- Docs: short internal README for updating shape catalog + policy_version bump process (owners: Ethan + Irene).
comments: 2025-02-03 (Ethan Park): Drafted schema proposal (shape_id + tier_policy_version) and sent to Irene/Vanessa for review. Main point of debate: whether to store full CPU/RAM/NIC metadata in control plane vs only GPU tuple. I’m leaning to store the full shape record since Sales/CS keep asking for a single source of truth.

2025-02-05 (Irene Choi): +1 to full shape record, but please keep it minimal and don’t try to mirror every cloud provider field. Also need a clear process for region availability changes—fleet will own updating allowlists. For MIG, we should explicitly encode mig_profile per shape; we have had misconfigs in the past.

2025-02-08 (Mina Haddad): Please ensure tier policy object can be referenced by admission control (ENG-2206). Even if we don’t enforce burst params here, we need a canonical flag so runtime behavior matches contracts.

2025-02-12 (Vanessa Ortiz): Region allowlists must be treated as "can provision now" not "exists in theory". For Premium, initial allowlist should be conservative. Also note: some shapes are only available with NVLink (multi-GPU). Add nvlink_required boolean so we can gate multi-node plans later.

2025-02-14 (Ethan Park): Implemented soft validation behind dedicated_shape_catalog_validation_v1; staging enabled. Backfill job mapped 87/92 deployments; 5 are ambiguous legacy configs (mixed A100 40GB vs 80GB fields missing). Created a follow-up list for manual resolution; will block tier changes on those once hard validation is on.

2025-02-18 (Sergio Costa): FYI for dashboards: please emit a counter for validation failures with reason labels; we can add a small panel to catch bad Terraform rollouts. Not paging, but we want visibility.

2025-02-20 (Ethan Park): Ready for review. Remaining items before merge: tighten error messages to be customer-safe (no internal region codes leaking?), and confirm initial Premium region_allowlist with Infra (waiting on Irene signoff).
